purpose: Machine-readable mirror of the decision rules in skill/SKILL.md, used by scripts/check_routing_reachability.py to audit which model x effort x mode combinations the rules can and cannot produce, and by scripts/check_policy_sync.py to prove this mirror and the shipped SKILL.md still describe the SAME rules. Nothing reads this at runtime; skill/SKILL.md remains the single source of truth for routing.
drift_guard: Every entry under `rules` carries `skill_md_assertion` (substrings that MUST appear in skill/SKILL.md) and, where a rule replaced an older one, `skill_md_must_not_appear` (the superseded wording). `scripts/check_policy_sync.py` fails if the marker version, the assertions or the negative assertions disagree with skill/SKILL.md. Change a rule here without changing SKILL.md and it fails; change SKILL.md's rule text without updating this file and it fails too. This exists because the audit once spent a whole pass validating iteration-18 while the shipped skill still implemented iteration-17.
not_shipped: Deliberately lives under evals/, not skill/. build-claude-ai-zip.ps1 ships only SKILL.md, reference.md, benchmarks.json and benchmark_frontiers.json, so this file adds nothing to the runtime package.

support_matrix.note: What the PRODUCT supports, verified against the sources recorded in reference.md 3 (Claude effort support), 9.3 (Codex effort mechanics), 9.8 (Astra) and 18 (GPT-6.1 Sol). 'unsupported' here is a capability limit, never a routing preference -- the router may not emit an unsupported cell even if a rule asked for it.

Haiku 4.5.note: no effort parameter at all; ultracode needs xhigh support, which Haiku has not

Sonnet 5.5.note: also the execute half of opusplan. Anthropic (Sonnet 5.5 prompting guide): `between_tools` thinking is rejected at xhigh/max -- irrelevant to routing, recorded because it is a support fact

Opus 5.5.note: API default effort is medium (Opus 5 was high); adaptive thinking cannot be disabled. Fast mode (research preview) is Claude API only per the model docs; Claude Code's /fast on 5.5 is unverified

Luna.note: GPT-6 Luna. learn.chatgpt.com (30 Sep 2026): 'up to Max (not Ultra)'. The router only ever emits low (D=0); max needs a flagship (Rule M1).

Sol.note: GPT-6.1 Sol (gpt-6.1-sol, 29 Sep 2026): low..max, `none` and `minimal` rejected; learn.chatgpt.com lists 'Light to Ultra'. Terra and every GPT-5.6 model are legacy and not routed.

Astra.note: Ultra on Astra confirmed 10 Sep 2026; effort 'none' rejected at the API

cross_arm.ultracode: Claude Code setting. Never on the Codex arm.
cross_arm.ultra: Codex product mode. Never on the Claude arm.

derived_signals.note: Not new 0-3 axes. Each is a named diagnostic that R/D/W/C provably does not measure, and each maps to exactly one product mechanism. Added in the reachability calibration pass (iteration-18).

O.name: orchestration load
O.question: How many DIFFERENT KINDS of step must the SESSION sequence and re-enter -- discover/research, implement, author tests, run tests/build/lint, repair what they caught, sync docs or package?
O.high_when: three or more distinct kinds of step, including a verification step whose failures feed back into implementation
not: repeating ONE kind of step across many units -- that is W
the stages of the ARTEFACT being built. A four-stage data pipeline authored in one go is implement x4 plus verify: two kinds, not four. O is about the session's steps, never the deliverable's.
an investigation loop. Measure, hypothesise, re-measure is one kind of step iterated; a root-cause hunt is deep work, not orchestration, and routes to xhigh.

P.name: parallelisable strands
P.question: Does the work split into 3+ strands that proceed without waiting on each other and merge at the end?
P.high_when: 3+ strands, which may be targets (services, repos, vendors) OR work-kinds (two investigation branches is NOT enough -- three or more: compare alternative approaches side by side, prototype competing designs, run independent investigations)
P.not: one coherent decision sliced up after the fact. Splitting a monolith is ONE boundary decision, not four strands.
P.mutually_exclusive_with: indivisible_single_chain. A task that splits into 3+ independent strands is not one indivisible decision, so `ultra` and `max` can never co-occur. The corpus lint enforces this rather than trusting the labeller.

A.name: autonomy horizon
A.question: Does the task run autonomously for a long stretch with many tool loops before a human sees it?
A.high_when: the user states that an earlier flagship-tier run at xhigh or max already fell short. A long or unattended session is NOT that (iteration-19: the hours-of-unattended-execution limb was removed -- Anthropic's own same-harness table has Opus 5.5 at or above Fable 5.1 on all eight benchmarks it lists, Terminal-Bench 4.0 included).

escalation_ladders.note: A model change, never an effort change (Step 7 Rule 2). Each rung has its own trigger; the ladder is not climbed by difficulty alone. Iteration-20: Codex has no rung 2 -- Terra is gone and Sol is already the daily driver -- so its ladder is Sol -> Astra, reached only through rung 3.
escalation_ladders.rung_2_trigger: Claude only: user states the work is critical / must not be under-resourced / an earlier run fell short (Sonnet 5.5 -> Opus 5.5).
escalation_ladders.rung_3_trigger: A=high AND the dominant capability is on the flagship list AND the user states a flagship-tier run at xhigh or max already fell short. (iteration-19: 'or the session is an hours-long unattended agentic run' removed.)

ultracode.expr: duration_gt_30min AND (O == high OR (W == 3 AND D >= 2)) AND NOT indivisible_single_chain
ultracode.previous: W == 3 AND duration_gt_30min AND NOT (D == 3 AND R == 3)
ultracode.why_changed: W measures surface; ultracode buys workflow orchestration. Three separate defects in the old rule: (1) false negative on mid-width multi-phase work -- a 25-file implement/test/build/repair session got no orchestration because it was not 100 files wide; (2) false positive on mechanical width -- 150 files of one rename fired it at D=1, which is pure quota waste, so the width disjunct now carries a depth qualifier; (3) a dead zone at D=3 AND R=3 where ultracode was refused for depth while Rule E3 independently refused max, leaving irreversible 300-service migrations on a bare xhigh. The guard is now the same indivisible-single-chain test E3 uses, so the two rules can no longer refuse a task for contradictory reasons.

ultra.why_changed: Parallelism is not target count. Strands of work inside one job count too -- three candidate designs investigated or prototyped side by side is the same primitive as three independent services. The D==3 floor is kept on purpose: Ultra runs ~4 agents, so it costs ~4x, and at D<=2 the mid tier already clears the bar.

retired.rule_text: **N1 · Codex +1 notch.** When the task is writing or restructuring code across multiple dependent steps and the model is Terra or Sol, raise the Codex effort one rung, capped at `xhigh` on both models, and never lower a rung that another rule already set higher. Never on Astra. Claude is untouched.
retired.previous_expr: agentic_multistep_write AND model in [Terra, Sol] -> +1 rung, capped at xhigh, and NEVER downward
retired.revert: Restore the N1 block in skill/SKILL.md, the rule_blocks.N1 entry, and delete `notch` from check_routing_reachability.AFTER.

codex_notch.expr: none -- Codex takes the same effort as Claude from the shared D table
codex_notch.why_retired: The notch compensated for a MODEL-tier gap. Its basis was Terminal-Bench 4.0: GPT-5.6 Sol 37.3 vs Opus 5.5 66.4, ~29 points. On AA's same-page run GPT-6.1 Sol scores 56 against Opus 5.5's 60 and Sonnet 5.5's 64 -- 4-8 points, no interval. Independently, GPT-6.1 Sol's own curve is nearly flat above high (50 / 51 / 52 on AA v4.3.2, and OpenAI's DeepSWE has max BELOW high, 71.9 vs 75.2), so one more rung buys about a point at +22% cost, the shape Rule E3 already rejects. The rule was described as 'loosely, not strongly' benchmark-backed when it was introduced; with its basis gone it has none.
codex_notch.previous: agentic_multistep_write AND model in [Terra, Sol] -> +1 rung, capped at max on Sol / xhigh on Terra

max.expr: D == 3 AND R == 3 AND model in flagship_models AND indivisible_single_chain

retired.rule_text: **E4 · Astra swap.** When the dominant capability is agentic-code or terminal-tool and the rules would emit `Sol · max`, emit `Astra · xhigh` instead.
retired.previous_expr: dominant capability in [agentic-code, terminal-tool] AND the rules would emit Sol max -> emit Astra xhigh instead
retired.revert: Restore the E4 block in skill/SKILL.md, the rule_blocks.E4 entry, and delete `e4` from check_routing_reachability.AFTER.

E4.expr: none -- Sol max stays Sol max
E4.why_retired: E4 swapped `Sol max` for `Astra xhigh` on agentic-code / terminal-tool because AA v4.3 had Astra xhigh 53 @ $2.31 vs GPT-5.6 Sol max 47 @ $1.99 and ~27k vs ~78k output tokens. GPT-6.1 Sol max is 52 @ $0.72 at ~38k tokens against Astra's 53 @ $3.26 at ~27k (AA v4.3.2, same page): a point apart, 4.5x cheaper. Astra still leads Terminal-Bench 4.0 by 3 points (59 vs 56, no interval), so the swap is removed by the EFFICIENCY step, not because Sol wins on capability.

frontier_escalation.expr: A == high AND prior_run_fell_short AND capability in flagship_capabilities -> Opus 5.5 becomes Fable 5.1, Sol becomes Astra
frontier_escalation.previous: no explicit rung; Fable 5.1 was reachable only through the biology and 1000+ file gates
frontier_escalation.why_changed: Anthropic publishes the trigger verbatim ('if your evals at xhigh or max effort still fall short on demanding reasoning or long-horizon agentic work, move to Claude Fable 5.1'), and the old skill text called it 'consistent, no extra rule needed' -- which meant a user who SAID the flagship had already failed got the flagship again. Deliberately narrow: on the aggregate index Fable 5.1 is inside the equivalence band against Opus 5 at ~1.5x cost per task, so difficulty alone must never reach it. Iteration-19 narrowed it once more: A=high now means ONLY the stated shortfall. Opus 5.5 (22 Sep) beats Fable 5.1 on every row of Anthropic's own table (Terminal-Bench 4.0 66.4 vs 55.8, FrontierCode 54.4 vs 50.3, CursorBench 4.0 57.8 vs 51.8, GDPval-AA 1846 vs 1735, AutomationBench 40.0 vs 31.4, HLE 67.7 vs 65.6, TB-Science 58.7 vs 52.6, OSWorld 2.1 81.8 vs 80.7) at $4/$20 vs $10/$50, so duration cannot justify the jump. Anthropic's step-up criterion is kept.

uncertainty.expr: direction requires published CI, published SE, repeated-trial dispersion, or a benchmark-owner practical-significance threshold; otherwise UNRESOLVED
uncertainty.previous: a gap counted if it was large relative to the benchmark's own observed spread across the roster (compiled as 0.15 x spread)
uncertainty.why_changed: Observed spread is how far apart the models happen to sit, not how precisely either score was measured. On a two-row cell the spread IS the gap, so every comparison would 'win'. Removing it leaves `science` as the only capability with a certified direction -- which is the honest state of the published record, and is why the badge table's thin rows carry `low-confidence`.
uncertainty.compiler: scripts/compile_benchmark_frontiers.py DIRECTION_BASIS; the compiler raises SpreadFallbackResurrected if min_fraction_of_spread comes back

E1.expr: NEVER emit Sonnet 5.5 max; escalation is Sonnet 5.5 -> Opus 5.5 at the same rung
E1.why: AA v4.3.2: Sonnet 5.5 max 56 @ $7.60 (~193k output tokens/task) vs Opus 5.5 xhigh 56 @ $3.46 -- same score, 2.2x the cost. Anthropic footnote: Sonnet 5.5 scores lower at max than xhigh on FrontierCode. Sonnet 5.5's lower rungs are unpublished, so E1 claims nothing about them.

codex_tier.expr: D=0 AND W=0 AND C<=1 AND R<=1 -> Luna; otherwise Sol (Sol Ultra when P=high AND D=3); Astra only through the Daybreak gate, the 1000+ file gate, or rung 3 (A1)
codex_tier.previous: Luna / Terra (D<=2, or D=3 outside the flagship list) / Sol (D=3 on the flagship list); Astra through five gates plus E4
codex_tier.why_changed: GPT-6.1 Sol (29 Sep 2026, $2/$10, 1.05M context) is the Codex default, scores 52 @ $0.72 on AA v4.3.2 at ~38k output tokens, and dominates every GPT-6 Sol rung. Terra has no successor and is absent from OpenAI's current-recommended list. Two Astra gates lost their basis: the >=1M-token gate ('only Codex model with a verified >=1M window' -- Sol has 1.05M) and the computer-use gate (OSWorld 2.0 73.5 vs 71.4, 2.1 points on a tier C relay, at 7x the cost). The 1000+ file gate stays as a positioning call, flagged least-supported.

badge_direction.expr: BD1: >=2 independent measurements agree (>=1 tier A/B), none disagree; else efficiency -- except at R=3, where a single admissible measurement (a lean) decides
badge_direction.previous: the badge table was hand-authored from the compiler's UNRESOLVED cells with a provenance judgement
badge_direction.why_changed: Every cross-ecosystem cell against GPT-6.1 Sol is UNRESOLVED, so 'the direction of the strongest provenance' had become a judgement call that flipped whole rows. BD1 makes it a computed hint: scripts/compile_benchmark_frontiers.py badge_hint, asserted by test_frontier_compiler.py, cross-checked against the BADGE20 table here by test_reachability_tool.py. The R=3 clause keeps SKILL.md's standing instruction that at R=3 the bar for calling parity is widened and 'when genuinely unsure, take the stronger candidate': without it a cost tie-break would hand every high-risk architecture task to the cheaper arm on the strength of one Terminal-Bench row that points the other way.

mechanism_rows.expr: MECH1: Ultra -> Codex; ultracode (O=high) or opusplan -> Claude; a BD1 benchmark direction beats a mechanism; two mechanisms cancel
mechanism_rows.previous: only parallel-independent (Ultra) was a mechanism row; orchestration and opusplan were carried by the agentic-code / deep-reasoning rows that happened to favour Claude
mechanism_rows.why_changed: Those two rows now read Codex (efficiency) against GPT-6.1 Sol, which would have handed the badge to the arm with no orchestration mode on a task the router itself sends to ultracode. Symmetry: a mechanism the router puts on one arm's line is a capability only that arm has.

rule_blocks.note: Canonical one-block statement of each load-bearing derived-signal rule, keyed by the rule id marked in skill/SKILL.md as <!-- rule:ID -->...<!-- /rule:ID -->. scripts/check_policy_sync.py asserts each string here appears VERBATIM inside its marked block in SKILL.md. This is stronger than the loose skill_md_assertion quotations: the sentence that defines the rule cannot drift from the mirror without failing the build. When a rule changes, edit the block in SKILL.md and this string together.

blocks.S0: **S0 · blocked output.** A prompt blocked at Step 0 emits exactly one line, a `Clarify:` line naming the missing information as a question, and no `Claude:`, `Codex:`, `Evidence:` or badge line at all.
blocks.D3DIAG: **D3DIAG · diagnosis.** The coding column is written for building, so debugging scores on its own test: bounded diagnosis is `D=2`, and adversarial diagnosis is `D=3` when at least two of these hold — the root cause is non-local or depends on timing or ordering; reproduction is intermittent or environment-dependent; several plausible causes must be ruled out by constructing competing hypotheses; a local-looking fix could mask a deeper invariant violation.
blocks.P1: **P1 · parallelisable strands.** `P = high` when the work splits into three or more strands that proceed without waiting on each other and merge at the end. A strand may be an already-independent target (service, repo, vendor) or an independent work-kind (three candidate designs investigated or prototyped side by side). Two strands is not enough, and one coherent decision sliced up after the fact is never strands.
blocks.M1: **M1 · `max`.** Emit `max` only when `D = 3` and `R = 3` and the model is a flagship (Opus 5.5 / Opus 4.8 / Fable 5.1 / Mythos 5.1 / Sol / Astra) and the difficulty is one indivisible novel-design or formal decision. Otherwise `xhigh`.
blocks.A1: **A1 · frontier rung.** Opus 5.5 becomes Fable 5.1 and Sol becomes Astra only when the dominant capability is on the flagship list and `A = high`, where `A = high` means the user states that an earlier flagship-tier run at `xhigh` or `max` already fell short. A long or unattended session is not that statement.
blocks.O1: **O1 · orchestration load.** `O = high` when the session must run three or more distinct phases, where a phase is a stretch of work that produces a different kind of deliverable and whose output is consumed by a later phase. The phases that count are research, implementation, independent verification, packaging, data or schema migration, documentation, and triage. The whole edit-run-repair implementation loop is one phase, and tests you write for your own change are inside it.
blocks.UC1: **UC1 · `ultracode`.** Emit `ultracode` when the estimated duration is over 30 minutes and either `O = high` or (`W = 3` and `D >= 2`) and the difficulty is not one indivisible chain. Write `ultracode` in the effort field. Every model except Haiku 4.5.
blocks.B1: **B1 · evidence applicability.** A benchmark row takes part in the badge decision only if the capability it measures is one of the dominant tags named for this prompt in Step 2. Applicability is checked before evidence quality and before any tie-break, and a row that is not applicable does not enter the comparison at all, however strong its number.
blocks.BD1: **BD1 · direction without an interval.** A badge direction needs at least two independent measurements that agree — an independent evaluator's run, or a vendor's table that favours its rival — at least one of them tier A or B, and none that disagree. The same benchmark re-published on a second page is one measurement, a tie is not opposition, and an aggregate never counts. Otherwise the cell is decided by efficiency, except at R = 3, where a single admissible measurement still decides it: a lean is not parity.
blocks.MECH1: **MECH1 · mechanism rows.** Ultra on the Codex line, and `ultracode` driven by `O = high` or `opusplan` on the Claude line, each name something only one arm has, so each decides the badge for the arm that has it, unless the other capability row carries a benchmark direction under BD1, which wins. Two mechanisms on one task cancel, and the capability rows decide.

skill_md_must_not_appear: 3+ already-independent targets scanned side by side
large relative to the benchmark's own spread
the dominant capability is structured design/architecture
hours of unattended agentic execution or the user states
≥ ~1M-token corpus / "load the whole repo at once"
